frequency_question: How often does the federal administrative process for revoking a recognized accrediting agency successfully conclude within a tight calendar window (e.g., under two years)?
membership_rule: Includes any formal federal agency proceeding targeting the termination of a recognized national accrediting agency's status; excludes voluntary relinquishments or minor scope reductions.

cases.name: American Bar Association accreditation review proceedings (historical)
ACICS (Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools) termination proceedings
ACICS second termination and final deregistration

coverage_note: 3 named major contested agency-level accreditation termination battles; believed to represent the entire population of major institutional/professional accreditor death-penalty proceedings in this timeframe.
known_gaps: Lower-level advisory committee recommendations that did not reach final formal departmental revocation orders are excluded by the strict definition.
skeleton: Total administrative revocation attempts by the Department of Education involving major accrediting bodies over the modern regulatory era, divided into those that successfully completed full revocation cycles versus those that resulted in renewals or dragged past statutory clocks.
multiplier: 2 successful revocations out of roughly 3 major contested termination attempts over 30 years.
validity_reason: Administrative procedures act constraints and regulatory frameworks governing federal recognition of accreditors remain stable across multi-year presidential cycles.
